newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy launches dramatic airlift from Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy launches dramatic airlift from Albania.

text.p: Italian military helicopters swooped into Albania on Monday to evacuate 35 people trapped in the riot-torn southern port of Vlore on Monday amid fears that the small Balkan state was on the verge of civil war.
The lightning operation, in which the helicopters were on the ground for just eight minutes, took place shortly after Prime Minister Romano Prodi met ministers to discuss the crisis.
Security along Italy's southeastern coast was beefed up to try to prevent any exodus of illegal Albanian immigrants.
Fearful for the lives of foreigners caught in Vlore, which has been the scene of the worst violence in two months of unrest in Albania, Italy organised a dramatic emergency airlift.
The Italian foreign ministry said among those plucked out of the delapidated port were 20 Italians, four Germans, a Dutch citizen and 10 reporters from various other countries.

The Albanian government declared a state of emergency at the weekend and warned armed insurgents in the south of the country that they would be shot without warning unless they surrendered their weapons. All roads to Vlore are believed to be blocked.

Two Chinook transport helicopters picked up the small group of foreigners and brought them to the southern Italian port of Brindisi. The aircraft were escorted by two armed Scout combat helicopters stationed on an Italian navy frigate.
Vincenzo Petrone, head of the foreign ministry crisis unit, said 20 Italians, four Germans, one Dutch and at least three Greek nationals were among those evacuated.
Prodi held over an hour of talks on the Albanian crisis with Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta and Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano.
"From the meeting emerged a common concern about the political situation, public order and finances in the country," a statement from Prodi's office said.
It added that international institutions should organise a financial aid for Albania -- Europe's poorest country.

Rioting flared in January following the collapse of a string of hugely popular get-rich-quick investments schemes. Up to nine people were killed during fighting between demonstrators and the secret police in Vlore on Friday.

Massimo D'Alema, the leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), which is the largest party within Prodi's centre-left coalition, urged political forces within Albania to work together to try to resolve the crisis.

"The country is one step away from a true and proper civil war," D'Alema wrote in a statement. "Only a political solution with an agreement between all the parties can restore calm...and prepare the way for new elections."
The speaker of the lower house of parliament, Luciano Voplante, said the Italian mob had been involved in the bankrupt Albanian investment schemes.
"Italian lowlife operated in Albania meaning that we have somehow contributed to the current situation," he said.

Italy, which briefly occupied Albania during World War Two, lies a short distance across the Adriatic from the Balkan country and has seen an influx of illegal Albanian immigrants since the collapse of Stalinist rule.

The interior ministry put coastguards and police in south eastern ports on a state of alert at the weekend for a possible rise in illegal immigrants from Albania and sent a helicopter and additional boats to the area on Monday to beef up patrols.
Coastguards in the southern port of Bari reported no sightings of Albanian immigrants, saying bad weather conditions were probably deterring boats from putting to sea.
